readings.title: Scorned by the Worthless
readings.subtitle: Job laments that he is now mocked by the sons of men he once considered lower than his dogs.
readings.text: [Job 30:1] “But now they laugh at me, those younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with my sheep dogs. [2] Of what use to me is the strength of their hands, since their manhood power has perished? [3] They are dried up from lack and hunger, they flee to a parched land, formerly a waste and ruin. [4] They pluck <dn>את</dn> salt herbs by the bushes, and broom tree roots for their food. [5] They were driven out from among men, they shouted at them as at a thief, [6] to dwell in the gullies of wadis, holes of the ground and clefts. [7] Among the bushes they cry out, under the nettles they huddled together – [8] sons of fools, even sons without a name, they have been whipped out of the land.

readings.title: A Song of Derision
readings.subtitle: The outcasts now make Job their byword, emboldened because God has afflicted him.
readings.text: [Job 30:9] And now I have become their song, and I am a byword to them. [10] They have loathed me, they have kept far from me, and did not refrain from spitting in my face. [11] Because <dn>He</dn> has loosed <dn>את</dn> my bowstring and afflicted me, they have thrown off restraint in my presence. [12] At my right hand a brood rises; they pushed away my feet, and they raise up against me their destructive ways. [13] They have broken up my path, they gain by my ruin; no one restrains them. [14] They come as through a wide breach; rushing on me under the ruins. [15] Destructions are turned upon me; they pursue my life as the wind, and my welfare has passed like a cloud.

readings.title: An Appeal to a Cruel God
readings.subtitle: Job describes his intense physical suffering and accuses God of becoming his enemy.
readings.text: [Job 30:16] And now my life pours itself out; days of affliction seize me. [17] My bones have been pierced in me at night, and my gnawings never lie down. [18] By great exertion is <dn>את</dn> my garment changed – it girds me as the collar of my coat, [19] throwing <dn>את</dn> me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes. [20] <dn>I</dn> cry out to <dn>You</dn>, but <dn>You</dn> do not answer <dn>me</dn>; <dn>I</dn> stand up, but <dn>You</dn> only look at <dn>me</dn>. [21] <dn>You</dn> have become cruel to <dn>me</dn>; with the power of <dn>Your</dn> hand <dn>You</dn> oppose <dn>me</dn>. [22] <dn>You</dn> lift <dn>me</dn> up to the wind, making <dn>me</dn> to ride it; and <dn>You</dn> melt <dn>me</dn> in a storm. [23] For <dn>I</dn> have known that <dn>You</dn> bring <dn>me</dn> to death, and to the house of appointment for all living.

readings.title: From Light into Darkness
readings.subtitle: Contrasting his past compassion with his present misery, Job's joy has turned to mourning.
readings.text: [Job 30:24] Yet does not one in a heap of ruins stretch out his hand, or in calamity cry out for help? [25] Did I not weep for him who was in trouble? Was my being not grieved for the poor? [26] When I looked for good, then evil came to me. And when I waited for light, darkness came. [27] My inward parts boiled and did not rest; days of affliction went before me. [28] I went about blackened, but not by the sun; I stood up in the assembly, I cried for help. [29] I became a brother of jackals, and a companion of ostriches. [30] My skin became black upon me, and my bones burned with heat. [31] So my lyre becomes mourning, and my flute the sound of weeping.

readings.title: An Oath of Moral Purity
readings.subtitle: Job swears he has made a covenant with his eyes and has not walked in falsehood or lust.
readings.text: [Job 31:1] “<dn>I</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> a covenant with my eyes. How then could <dn>I</dn> gaze at a maiden? [2] For what is the portion of <dn>Eloah</dn> from above, and the inheritance of <dn>the Almighty</dn> from on high? [3] Is it not calamity to the perverse, and strangeness to the workers of wickedness? [4] Does <dn>He</dn> not see <dn>את</dn> my ways, and number <dn>את</dn> all my steps? [5] If <dn>I</dn> have walked with <dn>את</dn> falsehood, or if my foot has hurried to deceit, [6] let <dn>Him</dn> weigh <dn>me</dn> in a right scale, and let <dn>Eloah</dn> know <dn>my</dn> integrity. [7] If my step does turn from the way, or my heart has gone after my eyes, or if <dn>את</dn> any spot has clung to my hands, [8] let me sow, and another eat; and let my harvest be rooted out. [9] If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or if <dn>I</dn> have lurked at my neighbour’s door, [10] let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down over her. [11] For that would be a wicked scheme, and a punishable crookedness. [12] For that would be a fire that burns to destruction, and take root among all my increase.

readings.title: An Oath of Social Justice
readings.subtitle: He declares his fair treatment of servants and his consistent care for the poor, the widow, and the fatherless.
readings.text: [Job 31:13] If <dn>I</dn> have refused <dn>את</dn> the plea of my male servant or my female servant when they complained against me, [14] then what should <dn>I</dn> do when <dn>Ěl</dn> rises up? And when <dn>He</dn> punishes, what should <dn>I</dn> answer <dn>Him</dn>? [15] Did not <dn>He</dn> who made <dn>me</dn> in the womb make him? And did not One fashion us in the womb? [16] If <dn>I</dn> have withheld <dn>את</dn> the poor from pleasure, or caused the widow’s eyes to fail, [17] or eaten <dn>את</dn> my piece of bread by myself, and the fatherless did not eat of it – [18] but from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother’s womb <dn>I</dn> guided her – [19] if <dn>I</dn> have seen <dn>את</dn> anyone perish for lack of garments, or a poor one without covering; [20] if his loins have not blessed me, and he warmed himself with the fleece of my sheep; [21] if <dn>I</dn> have raised <dn>את</dn> my hand against the fatherless, when <dn>I</dn> saw <dn>I</dn> had help in the gate; [22] let my arm fall from my shoulder, and my arm be broken from the bone. [23] For <dn>I</dn> am in dread of destruction from <dn>Ěl</dn>, and from <dn>His</dn> excellence <dn>I</dn> could not escape.

readings.title: An Oath Against Idolatry and Deceit
readings.subtitle: Job denies trusting in wealth, worshipping celestial bodies, rejoicing in his enemy's downfall, or hiding his sin.
readings.text: [Job 31:24] If <dn>I</dn> have put <dn>את</dn> my trust in gold, or called fine gold my refuge; [25] if <dn>I</dn> have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gained much; [26] if <dn>I</dn> have looked at <dn>את</dn> the sun when it shines, or the moon moving in brightness, [27] so that my heart has been secretly enticed, and my mouth has kissed my hand – [28] that too is a punishable crookedness, for <dn>I</dn> would have denied <dn>Ěl</dn> above. [29] If <dn>I</dn> have rejoiced when he who hated me was ruined, or lifted myself up when evil found him – [30] also <dn>I</dn> have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for a curse on his life – [31] if the men of my tent did not say, ‘Who is there that has not been satisfied with his meat?’ [32] The stranger did not have to spend the night in the street, for <dn>I</dn> have opened my doors to the way. [33] If <dn>I</dn> have covered <dn>את</dn> my transgressions like Aḏam, by hiding my crookedness in my bosom, [34] then let me fear the great crowd, and dread the scorn of clans, then <dn>I</dn> would be silent, and go out of the door!

readings.title: A Final Challenge for an Answer
readings.subtitle: Job signs his testimony, wishing for a written indictment from his accuser, and swears his innocence regarding the land.
readings.text: [Job 31:35] Who would give me a hearing? See, my signature, let <dn>the Almighty</dn> answer <dn>me</dn>, and let my accuser write a bill! [36] Would <dn>I</dn> not take <dn>את</dn> it up on my shoulder, bind it on <dn>me</dn> for a crown? [37] <dn>I</dn> would declare to <dn>Him</dn> <dn>את</dn> the number of my steps – <dn>I</dn> would approach <dn>Him</dn> like a prince. [38] If my land cries out against me, or its furrows weep together; [39] if <dn>I</dn> have eaten <dn>את</dn> its fruit without payment, or caused its owners to die; [40] let thistles grow instead of wheat, and useless weed instead of barley.” The <dn>את</dn> words of Iyoḇ are ended.
